analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown - November 6, 2026
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell 2.7% on the week amid a volatile post-midterm market. The trigger was concern that opposition to data center development could widen the supply-demand gap in the AI supply chain.
Gold miners, ACA beneficiaries and homebuilders outperformed. Memory, optical networks and oil logged the largest losses.
GS Prime data shows US equities modestly net sold, driven by the largest single-stock net selling in 4 months and partly offset by buying in Macro Products.
Info Tech was by far the most net sold global and US sector. The week's percentage selling in global Info Tech was about on par with the largest net-selling weeks on record (since 2016).
Hedge funds sold US Industrials at the fastest pace since Covid (April 2020).

Semis rose about 3.5% on Friday. The desk called it 'healthy' and not just a beta squeeze. Activity was extremely quiet and inbound client interest was focused on sentiment, with little follow-through.
Long-only funds were moderate net sellers on a steady drumbeat of semis supply. Hedge funds finished net buyers, driven by a Friday cover bid on macro expressions.

Systematic/CTA signals are negative in about 60% of global equity markets at short and medium-term horizons, including the S&P. GS expects CTAs to sell $28bn of SPX futures over 1 week and $45bn over 1 month in the baseline scenario, which would take the position to net short. The relevant S&P trigger levels are around 7685 and 7550.
Thursday saw an extreme volatility repricing. Clients had taken off protection into Wednesday's post-midterm relief rally and were underhedged going into Thursday's reversal.
GS's vol panic index surged to 9.57 out of 10. That was the 3rd largest daily jump ever, following the 4th largest daily drop on Wednesday. The combined two-day swing was the largest on record.

US-listed ETFs had their third largest day of notional volume on Thursday at $580 billion, 33% of the tape against a 28% average. On Friday morning ETFs were 36% of the tape, with dollar volumes up 65% vs the 20-day average.

GS desk likes shorting its Diversified Staples Basket (GSXUSTAP). Its earnings and dividend yields are unattractive relative to fixed income, growth is insufficient for the valuation, revisions are rolling over, and valuations sit in the 90th percentile relative to the last year.

GSXUSTAP has outperformed SPX by nearly 20% in the last month and is now up 1% more than SPX over the last year. Historically, Staples have lagged over the following 3 months after similar events, except in late 2021 and early 2022.

TMT: the NDX closed down about 5% on the week and is on a 4-week losing streak. The SOX fell 28% over 22 days, one of the largest rolling 1-month drawdowns in history, and semiconductor valuations are nearly 50% off the highs.

TMT: earnings were a sideshow as focus stayed on risk reduction and recalibrating data center build expectations after the midterm election. Investor conversations turned toward what is priced in for capex (gigawatt) builds, more 2028+ than 2027.
TMT: the desk sees a potential path higher for Tech and risk appetite around earnings (NVDA still to report), financing visibility, oil and rates relief, lowered expectations and reset positioning.

Financials rose 1.6% and Real Estate rose 2.8%, but day-to-day divergences between defensives and offensives reflected pricing in weaker growth from a potentially stalled AI capex buildout. Consumer payment companies were strong while lodging REITs were weak.
Subprime consumer credit datapoints were negative. UPST noted worsening macro conditions in 3Q and 4Q, and CACC signaled underperformance in its lower-score customers.
Industrials fell 260bps on the week and Materials fell 100bps. Homebuilders rose over 400bps while technology fell over 400bps.
Squeezes in small-cap, highly levered consumer names: JBLU +30%, DFH +27%, GPK +26%. VNT rose 16% and SWK 12% on earnings.
Data center related names fell sharply. LGN fell 27%, FPS, MOD and VRT about 22%, OEC fell 26% on poor earnings and KMT fell 21%. STRL and ECG were also named among the decliners.

Heavy de-risking and a sharp semis drawdown, with the desk seeing a potential path higher around earnings, financing visibility, oil and rates relief and reset positioning.
Financials rose 1.6% with sharp divergences between defensives and offensives, and negative subprime consumer credit datapoints.
Real Estate rose 2.8%, with healthcare REITs strong and lodging REITs weak.

earnings_insights: Earnings were described as a sideshow last week as attention stayed on risk reduction and data center build expectations.
NVDA earnings are still to come and are cited as a potential catalyst for Tech.
OEC fell 26% and KMT fell 21% on poor earnings results (reported the week of Nov 2).
VNT rose 16% and SWK rose 12% on straggler earnings that performed well.
UPST noted worsening macro conditions in 3Q and 4Q, and CACC signaled underperformance in its lower-score customers.
The tail end of earnings is next week. Conference season starts after that: NAREIT in two weeks and the GS Financials Conference in early December.

risk_factors: Opposition to data center development could widen the supply-demand gap in the AI supply chain.
A potentially stalled AI capex buildout could weaken economic growth.
Systematic/CTA selling could take the position to net short if S&P levels near 7685 and 7550 break.
Subprime consumer credit is deteriorating, per UPST and CACC commentary.
Investors are unsure when they will find out the path of data center capex, in the desk's words 'when do we find out'.

tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the S&P short and medium-term CTA levels around 7685 and 7550 would extend systematic selling.
